Hello Jeffrey,

Prior to my move to Germany, I had played Jyhad/V:TES in Omaha upon
it's inital release. When I did finally arrive in Germany, I was
tasked to locate and build a new gaming group within the area. Still
building and locating, but have succeeded in forming a group.

Wanting to set the group here on the right track insofar as playing I
started my investigation of the new Errata and Rulings that had cropped
up during my removal from the game (6 to 7 months). It too was a shock
to see the new Errata that had been set down. But in order to
participate within the Tournaments located throughout Europe I am
placed into a position of having to accept the rulings to allow the
players within my group a fighting chance within the V:TES community at
large.

To start, I do agree with you on the Wake with Evening's Freshness
(WwEF). However, I have already been around the bend on this and the
approach you are taking is bound to start a "Flame War" with some of
the more respected voices here within the Newsgroup... Peter Bakija,
James Coupe, Carl Pilhatsch, LSJ, just to name a few.

The WwEF ruling was determined to be viable change after the release of
Forced Awakening (Sabbat) which has a blood cost attached if the minion
being so awakened does not block the action. This in turn gave the
WwEF card too much capability for free. (The ability to cycle a card
for nothing except the loss of the Wake.)

Card limits has not been identified as the norm within the V:TES
community. The game was initially exempt from card limits and still
retains this ruling. This does not preclude the use of House Rules
that impose card limits, however. Talk of getting some tournaments
sanctioned by the DCI with card limits has been initiated and from my
understanding still being discussed. So do not worry about the card
limit issue.

On Voting, when a vote is initially played that card (the vote action)
may be replaced as the both predator and prey now have the option of
blocking the action. After the conditions of the vote are set down and
actual votes being tallied, no cards can be replaced. Additionally,
only one (1) political action card can be used by any Methuselah to use
in the vote. The inital political card used by the acting Methuselah
is only political action card that Methuselah can play. This does not
preclude the use of Action Modifers or Reaction cards being played,
just the political action cards.

On the issue of Return to Innocence, the card is banned with in DCI
tournaments and therefore a mute point. If you really wish to continue
using the card in it's printed capacity, do so. I personally do not
see anything wrong with the card. It is strong, yes, but constructed
deck tournaments tend to have a larger number of Deflections and
Telepathic Misdirections built in the decks than what I am use to
seeing. So I am not entirely sure as to why the card received errata
in the first place. But as I stated before, it is banned in DCI
tournaments.

The Archon Investigation still works as advertised, the last time I
looked. So, I am unsure as to where your complaint is on this card.

The No Repeat Action rule is something I have never investigated. I
currently work under the rule to better prepare my group for
tournaments. It was a welcome relief from the S:CE decks and repeat
bleed offenders. For local rules within your community, play as you
wish. But if you ever want to play in the tournaments that are
steadily increasing around the world :) swallowing your pride and
trying the new rulings is the only way to do it.

There are rulings that I do not agree with and my method of lobbying
has altered so the Newsgroups do not have to suffer with me. Find out
who are the Princes. Find out who are the dominate voices. And make
your inquiries with direct e-mail messages to help keep the wars down.

Sincerely,

Michael Eichler
Prince of Ramstein

The only card with no downside is Ascendance. One pool = one slot in
your deck = one master action. Even that's not quite accurate - in
practice, Ascendance has nothing BUT downsides. It's just that every
other master card's downsides are larger, but more specific, so you
build a deck to work around those downsides and take advantage of the
increased benefits. (Hunting Ground - costs two pool, but will
eventually gain more than Ascendance. True cost is time.)

>right don't use the other wake cards. If you want that many wakes in your
>hand as to be ridiculous well then, you'll wake and then what (no room for
>other cards, but you are waking like a champ).

This actually isn't true - if you have 25 wakes in your deck, you have
65 empty slots - PLENTY of room for other cards, and a lot of them can
be actions. Since you have 25 wakes, you have lots of actions
available to acquire things like intercept permanents, bleed
permanents, etc. Since you can freely cycle wakes, if you're screwed
at the end of your grandpredator's turn, you can Wake all your
vampires at once for his last action, fail to use Eagle's Sight and
block, reload your hand like a champ, and then deal with the NEXT
action with your handful of newly useful cards.

>2. Card limits - This subject has been beaten to death

Yes.

>3. Vote push - Push all you want, shame on you for playing a weenie vote
>push deck. This is also what max deck size is for. Exactly how was deck
>creativity measured?

Easy, all sorts of crazy shit has been either winning tournaments
and/or getting to the finals. I had an intercept deck in the finals
of the last tournament, and basically got hosed by seating position -
the two decks I didn't want to sit next to sat down before me, and the
two decks i *did* want to sit next to both deliberately sat away from
me. Shit happens, but when was the last time an intercept deck did
even THAT well? Rush decks have been consistently getting to the
finals in tournaments, and THAT is reasonably rare.

"Shame on you" is not a functional solution for tournaments. Some
people don't care. It's not REALLY functional for playgroups either
(decreases the size of the playgroup), but some people will anyway.

Max deck size? 90 cards? You only have to push 5 or 6 at a time for
the first few votes - after that you HAVE all the table votes you
need, and you only push votes when you run out of damage votes in your
hand. Too, TOO, too easy.

>4. RTI and AI - Intercept / deflect / reduce the bleed or die (no
>problems). Why, shouldn't you be bled for 11? Keep you pool high, rush
>your predators big guns, make a deal with someone to bash his 10 point
>vampire, play with the ravnos and reduce that stealth on the bleed and or do

Intercept is worthless against Day Op.

Reduce the bleed is worthless against a bleed of 16. (Arika's cap and
+2 bleed and a +3 Conditioning.)

Keep your pool high is worthless against a bleed of 16.

Rush is worthless against Arika - Obedience owns you HARD, or Skin of

Man, this seems like an overstatement about the ruling. "Hosed beyond
belief"?!? Just because you have to wait until untap phase to redraw
it? Hardly - IMHO, of course. I understand peoples' complaints about
the need (or lack thereof) for certain errata and the damage they feel
does to the game. But if the game could be reprinted from the ground up,
the errata on Wakeys are pretty much exactly how I'd redo the card. It's
well-balanced with Forced Awakenings now - to the point that I deliberately
used WWeF in some decks and FAs in others, depending on the type of deck.
This is exactly what you want.

I've found that in decks which don't have a lot of intercept in them and
don't stock a lot of combat cards, Wakeys are better than Forced Awakenings.
Your hand just doesn't miss the redraws before your next turn anyway.
(In such decks, most of the cards are used during *my* turn.) And you don't
want to wind up paying the extra blood if you fail to intercept or if you're
trying to do something besides intercept (e.g. Telepathic Counter or
Telepathic Misdirection). If you have intercept and combat, then yes,
the advantages of Forced Awakening start to become (somewhat) important
and its disadvantage disappears almost completely.

>BTW, I also agree that not every card must have a bad effect. If you
>put 20 WWEFs in your deck, how will be that much of a advantage?
>That's 20 card slots that could've gone to offensive instead of
>defense.

Actually, WWeF is more of an offensive card as long as your whole deck
isn't WWeF. This is because you're much freer to tap out and do something
to advance your position if you're holding one or two of them. Since there's
almost no drawback to the card *except* opportunity cost, I think it's
reasonable to make sure the opportunity cost lasts longer than to the end
of combat. Or even the end of an opponent's turn.

Fred

>2) Proxies of FA are not allowed in tournament play.

Accurate.

>3) Rather than being banned, WWEF was drastically altered. This
>causes confusion when teaching newbies. (Me teaching a newbie: "Forget
>about what it says. It really does this.")

Not drastically, since only the "when you replace" was altered. "next
untap" and "end of combat" do not alter the PRIMARY purpose of the
card - to allow a tapped vampire to react as if untapped.

> 3.5) Side note: since I was here (online and actively gaming), I
>hereby do attest that indeed virtually no discussion on this topic on

>this newsgroup took place *before* the ruling. Feel free to check out
>DejanNews to contradict me.
>

>really should only be played during your predator's turn. A case in
>particular is combat decks - reducing your hand size *drastically*
>decreases your ability to respond to or pose a threat.

Combat decks typically play with no Wakes and no FA's, as their
ability to survive depends directly on being pro-active. A combat
deck with enough intercept to block +2 stealth actions (one bleed + a
Lost in Crowds) probably hasn't got enough combat to kill things. A
combat deck with some Wakes thrown in can't stop anything at +1
stealth. The obvious solution is pack more Bum's Rush and quit
pretending that Wake, in ANY form, is useful in a combat deck. Ashes
take no actions.

In other situations, WWEF is hardly useless. Assuming it may only be
played during your predator's turn (not true, but)... this is a
problem why? 80% of the actions you wish to react to are going to
take place during your predator's turn. Using a FA instead of a Wake
may let you redraw, but you're still burning your untap-card like
crazy in the process. And that's assuming you successfully block and
don't cost yourself a blood.

>5) If played as is, or the modification "can't be replaced until end
>of acting player's turn", the opportunity cost will balance its
>effectiveness.

I have twenty-five Wakes in my deck, and through crappy draw, i have
five in my hand. On my grand-predator's turn, I pick an action at
random and spend four Wakes, one per vampire I possess, to find some
useful shit in my deck. What opportunity cost? ZERO! that's right,
ZERO. I just had to pick an action I couldn't block, which was
anything my grand-predator did. And I'm left with one Wakey and
probably five, maybe six useful cards. No no no no no no NO! Broken.

>I was somewhat surprised to see a previous post belittle the
>"opportunity cost" aspect of the game. It's my opinion that the
>majority of the game *IS* the opportunity cost of cards - with the
>remaining being a player's sequence of events and the metagame.

Correct. Wake, unerrata'd, has no opportunity cost.

significant cost, unlike every other card in the game. As Jyhad is a game of

Pre errata Wake had no such costs. Nada. Nothing. You had it in your hand you

change vote cards--and they errataed that rule too.

That is so not the point. Wake needed errata because it had a very significant
effect (it gave you extra actions) and had *zero* cost. Unlike every other card
in the game. As a result of its complete lack of cost, it could be cycled like
water--this was bad, but a result of its lack of cost. The only reason that the
free cycling was a problem was because Wake was a powerful card in and of
itself--it is always useful to be able to untap, but as opposed to all other
powerful but conditional use cards, it would never clog your hand, as you could
cycle it freely if you didn't need it, as it had no cost. If Wake had no other
function (like Deal with the Devil), who would care? If Wake's card text was
"Discard Wake to draw a new card", and it had no other use or cost, it would be
perfectly fine, although a complete coaster (unless 40 cards was too many for a
particular deck you have in mind...). That was not Wake's effect, however. It
had a very powerful effect, zero cost, and never clogged up your hand if you
didn't need it. Thus, too good.

Please compare pre errata Wake to Surprise Influence. Both are no discipline
reaction cards with no blood cost. Wake has a very commonly useful, powerful
effect. Surprise Influence has a occasionally useful, minimal effect.
Logically, Wake should be harder to use (i.e. have a higher cost) than SI, due
to the disparity in their effects for a similar card type. This is not the
case--Wake can be used and cycled freely, where SI has a very high conditional
cost (there needs to be a vote that someone else has called). This disparity of
cost indicates that something was wrong with Wake.

As to Deal with the Devil, DwtD has a perfectly reasonable cost (a master phase
*and* your entire hand) and its only effect is to allow you to redraw your
hand. It doesn't do anything else. It doesn't allow you to surgically cycle
your hand during your opponents turn as a side effect of its lack of cost. Wake
had a very useful effect, no cost, *and* the ability to be cycled for free.
Just too much. Hand cycling was not the problem with pre-errata Wake. It was
the complete lack of cost for a card with a powerful effect. The free hand
cycling was an added benefit and a symptom of somthing being amiss.

>>Vote cards. Uhm, wrong conversation. Don't want to start that argument
here.>>

Not that different of a conversation. Both effects were changed due to lack of
appropriate cost.

prevention or lots of tastes), and the inferior version is pretty much
worthless. As it isn't that easy to play, it is a bad idea to have more than 4

I'll accept that it is enough for you, but I assure you--Pulled Fangs that did
aggro damage was simply too powerful. It was a zero discipline card with no
blood cost that did aggrivated damage. What else did aggro damage in the
original set:

-Wolf Claws/CotD: Required a discipline. Cost a blood.
-Walk of Flame: Required a Discipline. Only worked second round.
-Burst of Sunlight: Required a Discipline. Did damage to you as well.
-Ivory Bow: Weapon. Fragile. Unique. Cost a pool. Required an action to equip.
Could be stolen/acquired.
-Sengir Dagger: Same as above, but cost 2 pool.
-Flame Thrower: Same as above. Cost 4 pool, but not unique.
-Dragon's Breath Rounds: Required a gun (see above). Destroyed that gun. Was
too good with Zip Gun. Thus, Zip Gun errataed.
-Body of Sun: Sucks plain and simple.

These are the cards that PF was built to be in line with. Even with the 1st
edition Aggro rules, it was too powerful when compared to these (and other
similar cost) cards.

PF was printed when a single point of aggrivated damage *could not burn a
vampire, ever*. When PF was printed, playing 8 of them on one vampire had
almost no greater effect than 1 (you still just went to Torpor--you just had to
grow back your fangs 8 times...). When the aggro rules changed, PF suddenly
became an unholy nightmare of a card, and far, far more powerful than
originally intended or designed. It needed to be fixed. Saying you could only
play one of them at a time simply does not fix the card. It is still too
powerful.

What possible justification can you come up with for a zero discipline, zero
cost card with low opportunity cost for being that powerful? Lucky Blow is also
a zero discipline, zero cost combat card. As is Dodge. The "Don't Redraw" and
"Do more damage" aspects of PF and Lucky Blow are a wash (and according to many
in the recent thread discussion, a single card slot is *very* valuable, making
the disadvantage of Lucky Blow an arguably more severe cost than the minimal
opportunity cost of PF...). What can possibly justify the fact that pre errata
PF is that much more powerful than Lucky Blow? That it is rare?
